display.purpose: Auth page hero line only — the one place Genesis pitches itself.

body.purpose: Chat messages and default UI copy.

label.purpose: Panel headings, tabs, badges, timestamps — uppercase structural text.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, sheets, and other true overlays only.

shadows.name: control-rest
shadows.purpose: Resting state of outline buttons and inputs — near-invisible, not a depth cue.

motion.name: panel-resize
motion.purpose: Workspace column width transitions when a panel is resized or collapsed.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single saturated call-to-action control in the system.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 7px; background: #e8bd62; color: #1b1914; font: 500 14px Geist, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #ecc677; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(232,189,98,0.5); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action button used throughout dialogs and toolbars.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid #34332d; border-radius: 7px; background: #11110f; color: #eeeae0; font: 500 14px Geist, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #1d1c18; border-color: #454339; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(232,189,98,0.5); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Single-line field used across auth, project, and settings forms.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 36px; width: 100%; padding: 4px 12px; border: 1px solid #3a382f; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: #eeeae0; font: 14px Geist, sans-serif; transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #8c8980; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #e8bd62; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(232,189,98,0.5); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Small pill used for connection/generation status; amber border+text when active, neutral otherwise.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border: 1px solid #44423b; border-radius: 999px; padding: 2px 8px; background: #1c1c18; color: #c6c1b7; font: 11px Geist, sans-serif; } .ds-badge-active { border-color: #6a562d; color: #f0c66e; }

components.name: Panel Card
components.description: Base container used for connection rows, project rows, and dialog bodies — flat, hairline-bordered, one tone above its background.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; padding: 16px 18px; border: 1px solid #34332d; border-radius: 9px; background: #171714; } .ds-card strong { font: 500 12px Geist, sans-serif; color: #eeeae0; } .ds-card span { font: 11px Geist, sans-serif; color: #8c8980; }

components.name: Panel Heading Label
components.description: Uppercase monospace micro-label marking a panel's identity — the system's structural-vs-content signal.
components.css: .ds-label { display: inline-block; color: #8c8980; font: 600 10px/1.4 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; }

narrative.overview:
Genesis looks like a tool-maker's bench, not a marketing surface: dark and unfussy, every panel earns its place, and the one warm accent color marks what's active or worth touching — the way a marked tool stands out on a dark workbench. There is exactly one theme (always dark; no light mode, no toggle) because the product is a working console, not a brand showcase. Chrome recedes — hairline borders, stepped near-black surfaces, uppercase monospace micro-labels — so the three things that actually matter (chat, code, live preview) can sit side by side without competing for attention.

The system rejects: light backgrounds, decorative gradients or illustration, multiple accent colors, drop shadows as a default depth device, and centered/marketing-style page compositions anywhere inside the authenticated app.
keyCharacteristics: Always-dark, single-theme — depth from tonal steps, not shadows
One accent (Signal Amber) used only for what's active, primary, or needs attention
Dense, monospace micro-labels doing structural/status work (IBM Plex Mono, uppercase, wide tracking)
Geist for everything a human reads at length; monospace for everything a human scans
Compact controls (28–40px control heights, 5–9px radii) — instrumentation, not billboard

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Amber is the only saturated color in the interface. Every other surface is a shade of near-black; every other piece of feedback (error, muted, disabled) uses desaturated tones. If a screen needs a second "important" color, that is a sign the hierarchy is wrong, not that the palette needs a second accent.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Structure Rule
rules.body: If text is naming where you are or what state something is in (a panel heading, a tab, a status badge, a timestamp) it is uppercase IBM Plex Mono. If it is content a human wrote or is reading (chat prose, dialog descriptions, form labels-as-sentences) it is Geist.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A panel, card, or row is flat at rest. Reach for a shadow only for a true overlay (modal, sheet, popover) — never to add visual weight to something that sits in normal document flow.

dos: Do keep Signal Amber (#e8bd62) as the only saturated color anywhere in the authenticated app.
Do build depth from the three-step near-black tonal ladder (#11110f → #161613 → #1d1c18) plus hairline borders before reaching for a shadow.
Do set structural/status text (panel labels, tabs, badges, timestamps) in uppercase IBM Plex Mono; keep everything a human composes or reads at length in Geist.
Do keep controls compact (28–40px heights, 5–9px radii) — this is an instrument panel, not a marketing page.
donts: Don't introduce a light theme or a theme toggle — Genesis is deliberately always dark.
Don't add a second accent hue; a new "important" color signals a hierarchy problem, not a palette gap.
Don't apply drop shadows to panels, cards, or rows that sit in normal document flow — reserve shadows for true overlays (dialog, sheet, popover).
Don't carry the dense workspace grid's tight spacing into the editorial auth/dashboard pages, or vice versa — the two layout registers are intentionally different.
